source_text: Infantes neque Dei arma neque diaboli gerunt donec peccare possint. Gloria Deo. Amen.
thought_title: Infants bear neither armor until they can sin
orientation: Origen is contrasting the armor of God and the armor of the devil, and now says that infants bear neither until they are able to sin.
pass_a_gloss: Infants neither [the] weapons of God nor [the] weapons of [the] devil [they] bear until [they] are able to sin. Glory [be] to God. Amen.

choices.why: Literal rendering of the Latin noun, preserving the subject's age and incapacity.
Keeps the military sense of the contrast between God's and the devil's equipment; 'armor' is reserved for lorica in the glossary.
Literal sense of carrying or wearing equipment, matching the soldier imagery.

choices.english: until they are able to sin
choices.why: Preserves the temporal clause and the subjunctive of possibility exactly.
rejected: as long as they cannot sin

pass_b_english: Infants bear neither the arms of God nor the arms of the devil until they are able to sin. Glory to God. Amen.
